items.t: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria (syrup: adults and children over 2 years).

src.q: indicated for the symptomatic treatment of allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria
in adults and children over the age of 2 years

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPCs accessed (tablets and syrup).

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: 10 mg once daily (1 tablet or 10 ml syrup).

src.q: Adults: One tablet once daily.
Adults and children over 12 years of age: 10ml (10mg) of the syrup once daily.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: no dose change.

src.q: No dosage adjustments are required in the elderly.
No dosage adjustments are required in patients with renal insufficiency.

items.t: Tablets: children 6 years and over weighing more than 30 kg: 10 mg once daily. Younger or lighter children: other formulations are more suitable.

src.q: Children 6 years of age and older with a body weight greater than 30 kg: One tablet once daily.
For appropriate dosing in children younger than 6 years or with body weight of 30 kg or less, there are other formulations more suitable.

items.t: Syrup, children 2-12 years by weight: more than 30 kg: 10 ml (10 mg) once daily; 30 kg or less: 5 ml (5 mg) once daily.

src.q: Children 2 to 12 years of age are dosed by weight
5ml (5mg) of the syrup once daily

items.t: Under 2 years: safety and efficacy not established; no data.

src.q: in children under 2 years of age has not been established. No data are available.
Children under 2 years of age: The safety and efficacy of Clarityn Allergy Tablets have not been established.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to loratadine or any excipient.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Severe liver impairment: use with caution; lower starting dose (see hepatic).

src.q: should be administered with caution in patients with severe liver impairment

items.t: Tablets contain lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take them.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine

items.t: Syrup contains maltitol and sorbitol: patients with hereditary fructose intolerance should not take it.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance should not take this medicine

items.t: Stop at least 48 hours before skin tests.

src.q: should be discontinued at least 48 hours before skin tests

items.t: CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors may raise loratadine levels and increase adverse events. Ketoconazole, erythromycin and cimetidine raised levels in trials without clinically significant changes (including ECG).

src.q: Potential interaction may occur with all known inhibitors of CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 resulting in elevated levels of loratadine
which may cause an increase in adverse events

Increase in plasma concentrations of loratadine has been reported after concomitant use with ketoconazole, erythromycin, and cimetidine in controlled trials, but without clinically significant changes (including electrocardiographic).

items.t: Alcohol: no potentiation in psychomotor studies.

src.q: have no potentiating effects as measured by psychomotor performance studies

items.t: No dose change in renal insufficiency.

src.q: No dosage adjustments are required in patients with renal insufficiency.

items.t: Severe liver impairment: start lower, 10 mg every other day (adults and children over 30 kg); syrup in children 30 kg or less: 5 mg (5 ml) every other day.

src.q: Patients with severe liver impairment should be administered a lower initial dose because they may have reduced clearance of loratadine.
An initial dose of 10mg every other day is recommended for adults and children weighing more than 30kg.
for children weighing 30kg or less, 5ml (5mg) every other day is recommended

items.t: SmPC: large data (over 1000 outcomes) show no malformations or fetal/neonatal toxicity, but as a precaution it is preferable to avoid in pregnancy.

src.q: A large amount of data on pregnant women (more than 1000 exposed outcomes) indicate no malformative nor feto/ neonatal toxicity of loratadine.
As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of Clarityn Allergy Tablets during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: loratadine can be used in pregnancy. SPS: if topical treatment fails, loratadine and cetirizine are the preferred oral antihistamines.

src.q: Loratadine can be used during pregnancy.
Loratadine and cetirizine are the preferred antihistamines for pregnant women.

items.t: SmPC: excreted in breast milk; not recommended when breastfeeding.

src.q: Loratadine is excreted in breast milk. Therefore, the use of Clarityn Allergy Tablets is not recommended in breast-feeding women.

items.t: SPS: a preferred antihistamine in breastfeeding; use with caution and monitor the infant for drowsiness, irritability, poor feeding and poor weight gain.

src.q: Loratadine is a preferred choice during breastfeeding, but infant monitoring is still required.
monitor the infant for potential side effects including drowsiness, irritability, poor feeding and inadequate weight gain

items.t: Fertility: no data.

src.q: There are no data available on male and female fertility.

items.t: Adults: most frequent above placebo were somnolence (1.2%), headache, increased appetite and insomnia. Children 2-12 years (common): headache, nervousness, fatigue.

src.q: The most frequent adverse reactions reported in excess of placebo were somnolence (1.2%), headache (0.6%), increased appetite (0.5%) and insomnia (0.1%).
common adverse reactions reported in excess of placebo were headache (2.7%), nervousness (2.3%), and fatigue (1%)

items.t: Hypersensitivity including angioedema and anaphylaxis (very rare).

src.q: Very rare Hypersensitivity reactions (including angioedema and anaphylaxis)

items.t: Very rare: convulsion, tachycardia, palpitation, abnormal liver function.

src.q: Very rare Dizziness, convulsion
